prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1405; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for our claim file. Can you confirm you're okay to proceed?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Great. Can you walk me through what happened on the day of the collision?

A: I was driving home on a two-lane road in Houston, going maybe thirty miles an hour. A car coming the other way drifted into my lane while trying to pass a slower vehicle. I tried to swerve but we still hit nose to nose.

Q: Did you have time to brake before impact?

A: Yes, I hit the brakes hard, but there wasn't enough room. The airbags went off and I think my hands came up against the steering wheel.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I always do.

Q: Did you or anyone else get out of the vehicle at the scene?

A: I got out on my own. The other driver was shaken up but walked around. A police officer came and took a report.

Q: Do you know which hand or wrist was injured?

A: My left wrist. It swelled up almost right away and I couldn't move my fingers properly. I went to the emergency room later that evening and they took X-rays.

Q: Have you received a diagnosis for the wrist?

A: Yes, they said it was a fracture. I've been told I'll need a cast for several weeks and possibly physical therapy after that.

Q: Did you have any injuries besides the wrist?

A: A bit of neck soreness and a bruise on my chest from the seatbelt, but nothing serious.

Q: Is there anything you'd like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
